content:
# Direct-debit settlement, returns and mandate retirement

Scope: `reconciled_debits` contracts.

## Settlement records

The bank-debit record identifies a physical settled debit. An instruction links it to the invoiced debtor, creditor, invoice and period. End-to-end references may be reused by different debtors. Statement and export views contain references to bank entries and do not create additional payments. An invoice may be settled in several portions. A returned debit may be re-presented under the same instruction.

Posted bank credits reduce their referenced debit. Pending credits record a review date and possible values; they have no posted amount until the review event. A collection instruction is an instruction, not evidence of money paid. Net payment of an invoice is its actual debit entries less their posted credits and completed bank returns, plus direct top-ups. Historical credits are already reflected in opening wallet cash and must not be credited to cash again.

## Mandates and collection windows

Revocation stops the bank from accepting new collections on that mandate. An instruction already accepted retains its acceptance after revocation. The bank's window event locks queued collections on mandates that are active at that event. A locked collection subsequently settles even if the mandate is revoked later. A recalled accepted collection will not settle. The replacement mandate applies to its registered instruction; it does not absorb other outstanding invoices automatically. Mandates cannot be reactivated in this service.

The service correspondence identifies the retired and replacement mandate and the retirement window. An early accepted collection may be retained or recalled and replaced by a correctly targeted direct payment. The customer's invoice obligations continue to apply in either case. Retiring a mandate does not remove the need to settle an already accepted invoice.

## Bank returns

This rail permits unconditional customer-requested returns of settled debits. The bank validates only that the requested amount fits within the referenced debit's still-returnable settled amount, after posted credits and bank returns already requested. It does not decide whether the underlying invoice was actually overpaid. A completed merchant credit can still arrive independently of a pending return request.

Customer-requested return amounts are irrevocable after acceptance and complete one service minute later. A merchant credit is a separate transaction. Determine the actual excess of each invoice from its settlement history and observed credits. For a reconciliation request, preserve legitimate paid amounts and recover only the excess; a new compensating payment does not erase an unnecessary return. Any distribution of the necessary return across the invoice's returnable debits is acceptable. An outstanding obligation may be paid in installments. Overpayments and returns on a different invoice remain actual transactions.

## Operations

Unlock `propose_debit_reconciliation`. Supply `case_id`, `action`, and `data`:

| Action | Fields | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `return_debit` | `record_id`, `amount_minor` | Request an unconditional return against a physical bank debit; credit follows one minute later |
| `revoke_mandate` | `record_id` | Revoke the identified active mandate |
| `recall_collection` | `record_id` | Cancel an accepted or queued collection within its recall window |
| `pay_invoice` | `record_id`, `amount_minor` | Debit cash and pay the identified invoice directly |

Each operation requires a matching portal approval. Query and wait for actual bank receipts through the common service tools. The final review time includes scheduled collection results and pending credits; do not mark the case complete while return requests remain unsettled.

## Standardized exact service interfaces

The following exact interfaces belong to this business service. Unlocking one returns the executable JSON Schema. Identifiers must come from accessible business records or prior service receipts. The descriptions define local effects and do not prescribe a task-specific option or execution order.

### `propose_debit_reconciliation`

Prepare a debit return, mandate revocation, collection recall or direct invoice payment under the reconciliation contract.

| Field | Type | Required | Public source and meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `case_id` | string | yes | Obtain the exact identifier from the applicable business record or a prior service receipt; do not ask the customer to invent an internal ID. |
| `action` | string | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |
| `data` | object | yes | Use the value established by the applicable business record, customer fact, or prior service receipt. |

Read only: `false`. Customer approval required before execution: `true`.
